The standards in this chapter apply to diabetes 
mellitus as a chronic condition. The self-limiting 
condition known as gestational diabetes 
mellitus does not affect licensing. However, 
consideration should be given to short-term 
fitness to drive in women with gestational 
diabetes mellitus treated with insulin, although 
severe hypoglycaemia in this condition is rare. 
Affected women should be counselled to 
recognise symptoms and to restrict driving when 
symptoms occur.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person 
who reports or is suspected of experiencing 
diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation 
should be referred for assessment by an 
optometrist or ophthalmologist. For diplopia 
managed with an occluder, a three-month non-
driving period applies in order to re-establish 
depth perception.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)

licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

guideline_evidence.source_text:
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

3.2.4. Gestational diabetes mellitus
The standards in this chapter apply to diabetes 
mellitus as a chronic condition. The self-limiting 
condition known as gestational diabetes 
mellitus does not affect licensing. However, 
consideration should be given to short-term 
fitness to drive in women with gestational 
diabetes mellitus treated with insulin, although 
severe hypoglycaemia in this condition is rare. 
Affected women should be counselled to 
recognise symptoms and to restrict driving when 
symptoms occur.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person 
who reports or is suspected of experiencing 
diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation 
should be referred for assessment by an 
optometrist or ophthalmologist. For diplopia 
managed with an occluder, a three-month non-
driving period applies in order to re-establish 
depth perception.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

input_snapshot.nurse_note:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

guideline_evidence.source_text:
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

3.2.4. Gestational diabetes mellitus
The standards in this chapter apply to diabetes 
mellitus as a chronic condition. The self-limiting 
condition known as gestational diabetes 
mellitus does not affect licensing. However, 
consideration should be given to short-term 
fitness to drive in women with gestational 
diabetes mellitus treated with insulin, although 
severe hypoglycaemia in this condition is rare. 
Affected women should be counselled to 
recognise symptoms and to restrict driving when 
symptoms occur.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person 
who reports or is suspected of experiencing 
diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation 
should be referred for assessment by an 
optometrist or ophthalmologist. For diplopia 
managed with an occluder, a three-month non-
driving period applies in order to re-establish 
depth perception.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

guideline_evidence.source_text:
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

3.2.4. Gestational diabetes mellitus
The standards in this chapter apply to diabetes 
mellitus as a chronic condition. The self-limiting 
condition known as gestational diabetes 
mellitus does not affect licensing. However, 
consideration should be given to short-term 
fitness to drive in women with gestational 
diabetes mellitus treated with insulin, although 
severe hypoglycaemia in this condition is rare. 
Affected women should be counselled to 
recognise symptoms and to restrict driving when 
symptoms occur.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person 
who reports or is suspected of experiencing 
diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation 
should be referred for assessment by an 
optometrist or ophthalmologist. For diplopia 
managed with an occluder, a three-month non-
driving period applies in order to re-establish 
depth perception.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

messages.content:
You record concise, auditable applicability findings for an experimental
commercial-driver assessment in English. Do not produce an overall fitness outcome
in this stage. Evaluate EVERY supplied passage exactly once in supplied order.
These findings are model proposals, not established clinical facts.

Only verified_patient_facts establish patient findings. Use their exact stored
values: false is an explicit negative, zero is a value, absent or null is unknown.
The nurse note gives context only. Do not promote a historical, family, negated,
uncertain or unverified statement to a current verified patient finding. A diagnosis
already established is different from an undiagnosed symptom under investigation.
Do not infer loss of consciousness from tiredness alone.

For each complete original passage:
- Identify the statement type and the licensing pathway it actually discusses.
  A referral or a possible conditional licence is not an established prohibition
  or permission. Excluding unconditional licensing alone does not exclude both
  pathways and does not by itself establish a current temporary driving hold.
- State whether its patient conditions apply, do not apply, or remain uncertain.
  Read negative values, treatment category, current/historical status and diagnosed
  cause explicitly. An applicable passage may still have unmet prerequisites.
- Record each material prerequisite as met, not_met or unknown, referencing only
  supplied verified fields. Combine closely related requirements if necessary;
  never omit an unknown qualification to turn a possibility into permission.
- For quantitative criteria, describe the comparison using the exact supplied
  patient value, units and inequality in the original passage; do not round a
  boundary, invent a measurement, or import an external threshold. If no comparison
  is relevant write 'Not applicable'. If units or measurements are absent say so.
- Distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
  information_missing. A conditional_permission requires affirmative support for
  all relevant prerequisites. A treatment name alone is insufficient. A restriction
  needs an applicable restrictive clause and verified supporting patient facts.

Select only supplied passage IDs and fact fields. Keep each conclusion concise.
Do not copy the passage or provide private reasoning. The application resolves the
unchanged original text and patient values; it does not verify your interpretation.

guideline_evidence.source_text:
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

3.2.4. Gestational diabetes mellitus
The standards in this chapter apply to diabetes 
mellitus as a chronic condition. The self-limiting 
condition known as gestational diabetes 
mellitus does not affect licensing. However, 
consideration should be given to short-term 
fitness to drive in women with gestational 
diabetes mellitus treated with insulin, although 
severe hypoglycaemia in this condition is rare. 
Affected women should be counselled to 
recognise symptoms and to restrict driving when 
symptoms occur.

10.2.3. Diplopia
People suffering from all but minor forms of 
diplopia are generally not fit to drive. Any person 
who reports or is suspected of experiencing 
diplopia within 20 degrees from central fixation 
should be referred for assessment by an 
optometrist or ophthalmologist. For diplopia 
managed with an occluder, a three-month non-
driving period applies in order to re-establish 
depth perception.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods driver 
licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person with diabetes treated by diet and 
exercise alone may drive without licence 
restriction. They should he reviewed by their 
treating doctor periodically regarding the 
progression of their diabetes.
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence:
•	 if the person has non–insulin treated 
diabetes mellitus and is being treated with 
glucose-lowering agents other than insulin.
A conditional licence may be considered 
by the driver licensing authority subject to at 
least annual review, taking into consideration 
the nature of the driving task and information 
provided by an endocrinologist or consultant 
physician specialising in diabetes* on whether 
the following criteria are met:
•	 there is no recent history of a ‘severe 
hypoglycaemic event’ as assessed by the 
specialist; and
•	 the person experiences early warning 
symptoms (awareness) of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 the person is following a treatment regimen 
that minimises the risk of hypoglycaemia; 
and
•	 there is an absence of end-organ 
effects that may affect driving as per this 
publication.
* For a commercial driver with type 2 diabetes 
who is being treated with metformin alone, the 
annual review for a conditional licence may 
be undertaken by the driver’s treating doctor 
upon mutual agreement of the treating doctor, 
specialist and driver licensing authority. The 
initial granting of a conditional licence must, 
however, be based on information provided by 
the specialist.

Commercial standards
(Drivers of heavy vehicles, public passenger 
vehicles or requiring a dangerous goods 
driver licence – refer to definition in Table 3)
A person is not fit to hold an unconditional 
licence or a conditional licence:
•	 if the person experiences any diplopia 
(other than physiological diplopia) within 
20 degrees from central fixation.

input_snapshot.nurse_note:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

input_snapshot.nurse_note:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation.

Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan.   boundary, invent a measurement, or import an external threshold. If no comparison
  is relevant write 'Not applicable'. If units or measurements are absent say so.

unchanged original text and patient values; it does not verify your interpretation.

input_snapshot.nurse_note:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver has established diabetes. The current specialist letter confirms that diabetes is managed with insulin and that the diabetes is not gestational. The driver has been adjusting meal times around split shifts and sometimes receives a sensor warning before feeling symptoms, but there is no documented recent episode requiring another person's assistance and no complete assessment of hypoglycaemia awareness in the material provided.

The ophthalmologist confirms non-physiological diplopia following a recent examination. Diplopia is present within 20 degrees of central fixation. The driver says the double image is more noticeable after prolonged night driving, yet the specialist reproduced it during daytime testing, so its absence during a short nursing interview is not treated as proof that the documented finding has resolved.

A change of lenses has been proposed but not assessed, and the nurse has no updated specialist decision about the visual symptoms or the diabetes monitoring plan. The two confirmed findings are recorded independently; neither a successful lens adjustment nor adequate glucose control has been assumed.

You record concise, auditable applicability findings for an experimental
commercial-driver assessment in English. Do not produce an overall fitness outcome
in this stage. Evaluate EVERY supplied passage exactly once in supplied order.
These findings are model proposals, not established clinical facts.

Only verified_patient_facts establish patient findings. Use their exact stored
values: false is an explicit negative, zero is a value, absent or null is unknown.
The nurse note gives context only. Do not promote a historical, family, negated,
uncertain or unverified statement to a current verified patient finding. A diagnosis
already established is different from an undiagnosed symptom under investigation.
Do not infer loss of consciousness from tiredness alone.

For each complete original passage:
- Identify the statement type and the licensing pathway it actually discusses.
  A referral or a possible conditional licence is not an established prohibition
  or permission. Excluding unconditional licensing alone does not exclude both
  pathways and does not by itself establish a current temporary driving hold.
- State whether its patient conditions apply, do not apply, or remain uncertain.
  Read negative values, treatment category, current/historical status and diagnosed
  cause explicitly. An applicable passage may still have unmet prerequisites.
- Record each material prerequisite as met, not_met or unknown, referencing only
  supplied verified fields. Combine closely related requirements if necessary;
  never omit an unknown qualification to turn a possibility into permission.
- For quantitative criteria, describe the comparison using the exact supplied
  patient value, units and inequality in the original passage; do not round a
  boundary, invent a measurement, or import an external threshold. If no comparison
  is relevant write 'Not applicable'. If units or measurements are absent say so.
- Distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
  information_missing. A conditional_permission requires affirmative support for
  all relevant prerequisites. A treatment name alone is insufficient. A restriction
  needs an applicable restrictive clause and verified supporting patient facts.

Select only supplied passage IDs and fact fields. Keep each conclusion concise.
Do not copy the passage or provide private reasoning. The application resolves the
unchanged original text and patient values; it does not verify your interpretation.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

answer.explanation: The driver has a diagnosed visual field defect, which may impact their ability to drive safely. However, the driver's visual acuity is satisfactory in the better eye, and the driver has not had any other visual field loss that is likely to impede driving. The driver's optometrist has assessed that the driver may be safe to drive after consideration of the above factors. Therefore, the driver may be eligible for a conditional licence, pending further assessment and review.

criterion_checks.conclusion: may_meet_conditional_standard
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
For private vehicle drivers, a conditional licence 
may be considered by the driver licensing 
authority if the horizontal visual field is 110 
degrees and the visual acuity is satisfactory in 
the better eye. People with monocular vision are 
generally not fit to drive a commercial vehicle. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority if the horizontal visual 
field is 140 degrees, the visual acuity in the 
better eye is satisfactory, there is no other visual 
field loss that is likely to impede driving and an 
ophthalmologist/optometrist assesses that the 
person may be safe to drive after consideration 
of the above factors. The better eye must be 
reviewed at least every two years. 
If monocular automated static perimetry is 
undertaken on patients without symptoms, family 
history or risk factors for visual field loss, and 
shows no indication of any visual field concerns, 
this information may be sufficient to confirm 
that the standard is met. If monocular testing 
suggests a field defect, or if the patient has a 
progressive eye condition, and/or the patient 
has any other symptoms or signs that indicate 
a field defect, then binocular testing should be 
conducted using the Esterman binocular field 
test or an Esterman-equivalent test. Alternative 
devices must have the ability to monitor fixation 
and to stimulate the same spots as the standard 
binocular Esterman. 
Sudden loss of unilateral vision
A person who has lost an eye or most of the 
vision in an eye on a long-term basis has to 
adapt to their new visual circumstances and 
re-establish depth perception. They should 
therefore be advised not to drive for an 
appropriate period after the onset of their 
sudden loss of vision (usually three months). 
They should notify the driver licensing authority 
and be assessed according to the relevant 
visual field standard.

criterion_checks.conclusion: may_meet_conditional_standard
criterion_checks.guideline_quote:
1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.

input_snapshot.nurse_note:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver had transient loss of consciousness while seated after a delivery, with a colleague documenting failure to respond and a brief gap in recall. The current physician referral states that the mechanism is under investigation. An emergency differential mentions arrhythmia and seizure without confirming either, and a glucose measurement obtained after food cannot establish the cause of the event.

The optometrist confirms a visual field defect on a separate current signed assessment. The driver describes occasionally noticing vehicles late on the left, although central letters remain clear; a specialist has not yet documented whether the defect is stable, its complete binocular horizontal extent or whether other significant field loss is present.

An older report described satisfactory central acuity, but the nurse has not used it to overrule the newer field finding. The driver is unsure whether a remote dizzy spell involved loss of awareness, so the number of confirmed events and the appropriate event-free interval remain unresolved despite documentation of the recent event and the visual field defect.

Monocular drivers have a reduction of visual 
fields due to the nose obstructing the medial 
visual field. They also have no stereoscopic 
vision and may have other deficits in 
visual functions.

For private vehicle drivers, a conditional licence 
may be considered by the driver licensing 
authority if the horizontal visual field is 110 
degrees and the visual acuity is satisfactory in 
the better eye. People with monocular vision are 
generally not fit to drive a commercial vehicle. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority if the horizontal visual 
field is 140 degrees, the visual acuity in the 
better eye is satisfactory, there is no other visual 
field loss that is likely to impede driving and an 
ophthalmologist/optometrist assesses that the 
person may be safe to drive after consideration 
of the above factors. The better eye must be 
reviewed at least every two years. 
If monocular automated static perimetry is 
undertaken on patients without symptoms, family 
history or risk factors for visual field loss, and 
shows no indication of any visual field concerns, 
this information may be sufficient to confirm 
that the standard is met. If monocular testing 
suggests a field defect, or if the patient has a 
progressive eye condition, and/or the patient 
has any other symptoms or signs that indicate 
a field defect, then binocular testing should be 
conducted using the Esterman binocular field 
test or an Esterman-equivalent test. Alternative 
devices must have the ability to monitor fixation 
and to stimulate the same spots as the standard 
binocular Esterman.

and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is

Some drivers may attribute a crash or driving 
mishap to a ‘blackout’ to excuse an event 
that occurred for some other reason such as 
inattention or distraction (e.g. a mobile phone 
conversation). There will also be a small 
proportion of cases in which a clear cause 
cannot be established.

10.2.2. Visual fields3–6,8–13
For the purposes of this publication, visual 
fields are defined as a measure of the extent 
of peripheral (side) vision. Normal visual field is: 
60 degrees nasally, 100 degrees temporally, 75 
degrees inferiorly and 60 degrees superiorly. 
The binocular field extends the horizontal extent 
from 160 to 200 degrees, with the central 120 
degrees overlapping and providing the potential 
for stereopsis. 
Visual fields may be reduced due to a range 
of neurological conditions (e.g. stroke, multiple 
sclerosis) as well by ocular diseases (e.g. 
glaucoma), or injuries, resulting in hemionopia, 
quadrantanopia or monocularity. 
Peripheral vision assists the driver to be aware 
of the total driving environment. Once alerted, 
the central fovea area is moved to identify 
the importance of the information. Therefore, 
peripheral vision loss that is incomplete will 
still allow awareness; this includes small areas 
of loss and patchy loss. Additionally, affected 
drivers can adapt to the defect by scanning 
regularly and effectively and can have good 
awareness. Patients with visual field defects 
who have full intellectual/cognitive capacity 
are more able to adapt, but those with such 
impairments will have decreased awareness and 
are therefore not safe to drive.
A longstanding field defect, such as from 
childhood, may lead to visual adaptation. Such 
defects need to be assessed by an optometrist 
or ophthalmologist for a conditional licence 
to be considered. They should be managed 
as an exceptional case to the standard, with 
consideration for duration and evidence of visual 
adaptation, whether the location of the defect is 
an area that may already be blocked by the car 
door on the passenger side (i.e. the inferior field 
on the left side without central field loss), driver 
safety record and the nature of the driving task.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

may be considered by the driver licensing 
authority if the horizontal visual field is 110 
degrees and the visual acuity is satisfactory in 
the better eye. People with monocular vision are 
generally not fit to drive a commercial vehicle. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority if the horizontal visual 
field is 140 degrees, the visual acuity in the 
better eye is satisfactory, there is no other visual 
field loss that is likely to impede driving and an 
ophthalmologist/optometrist assesses that the 
person may be safe to drive after consideration 
of the above factors. The better eye must be 
reviewed at least every two years. 
If monocular automated static perimetry is 
undertaken on patients without symptoms, family 
history or risk factors for visual field loss, and 
shows no indication of any visual field concerns, 
this information may be sufficient to confirm 
that the standard is met. If monocular testing 
suggests a field defect, or if the patient has a 
progressive eye condition, and/or the patient 
has any other symptoms or signs that indicate 
a field defect, then binocular testing should be 
conducted using the Esterman binocular field 
test or an Esterman-equivalent test. Alternative 
devices must have the ability to monitor fixation 
and to stimulate the same spots as the standard 
binocular Esterman.

A person who has lost an eye or most of the 
vision in an eye on a long-term basis has to 
adapt to their new visual circumstances and 
re-establish depth perception. They should 
therefore be advised not to drive for an 
appropriate period after the onset of their 
sudden loss of vision (usually three months). 
They should notify the driver licensing authority 
and be assessed according to the relevant 
visual field standard.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

The driver describes occasionally noticing vehicles late on the left, although central letters remain clear; a specialist has not yet documented whether the defect is stable, its complete binocular horizontal extent or whether other significant field loss is present.

An older report described satisfactory central acuity, but the nurse has not used it to overrule the newer field finding. The driver is unsure whether a remote dizzy spell involved loss of awareness, so the number of confirmed events and the appropriate event-free interval remain unresolved despite documentation of the recent event and the visual field defect.

Methods of measuring visual fields are limited in 
their ability to resemble the demands of the real-
world driving environment where drivers are free 
to move their eyes as required and must sustain 
their visual function in variable conditions. 
Additional factors to be considered by the driver 
licensing authority in assessing patients with 
defects in visual fields therefore include, but are 
not limited to, the following:
•	
kinetic fields conducted on a Goldman
•	
binocular Esterman visual fields conducted 
without fixation monitoring, often referred to 
as a roving Esterman (two consecutive tests 
must be performed with no more than one 
false-positive allowed) – the test should be 
in the numeric field format when it is printed 
out or sent for an opinion
•	
contrast sensitivity and glare susceptibility
•	
medical history; duration and prognosis; 
if the condition is progressive; rate of 
progression/deterioration; effectiveness of 
treatment/management
•	
driving record before and since the 
occurrence of the defect
•	
the nature of the driving task – for example, 
type of vehicle (truck, bus, etc.), roads 
and distances to be travelled concomitant 
medical conditions such as cognitive 
impairment or impaired rotation of the neck.
There is no flexibility in this regard for 
commercial vehicle drivers. 
Monocular vision (one-eyed driver)
Monocular drivers have a reduction of visual 
fields due to the nose obstructing the medial 
visual field. They also have no stereoscopic 
vision and may have other deficits in 
visual functions.

1.2.4. Blackouts of undetermined 
mechanism
If, despite extensive investigation, the 
mechanism of a blackout cannot be determined, 
fitness to drive should be assessed according 
to section 1.3. Medical standards for licensing. 
The standards for blackout of undetermined 
mechanism are similar to those for seizure.

For private vehicle drivers, a conditional licence 
may be considered by the driver licensing 
authority if the horizontal visual field is 110 
degrees and the visual acuity is satisfactory in 
the better eye. People with monocular vision are 
generally not fit to drive a commercial vehicle. 
A conditional licence may be considered by the 
driver licensing authority if the horizontal visual 
field is 140 degrees, the visual acuity in the 
better eye is satisfactory, there is no other visual 
field loss that is likely to impede driving and an 
ophthalmologist/optometrist assesses that the 
person may be safe to drive after consideration 
of the above factors. The better eye must be 
reviewed at least every two years. 
If monocular automated static perimetry is 
undertaken on patients without symptoms, family 
history or risk factors for visual field loss, and 
shows no indication of any visual field concerns, 
this information may be sufficient to confirm 
that the standard is met. If monocular testing 
suggests a field defect, or if the patient has a 
progressive eye condition, and/or the patient 
has any other symptoms or signs that indicate 
a field defect, then binocular testing should be 
conducted using the Esterman binocular field 
test or an Esterman-equivalent test. Alternative 
devices must have the ability to monitor fixation 
and to stimulate the same spots as the standard 
binocular Esterman. 
Sudden loss of unilateral vision
A person who has lost an eye or most of the 
vision in an eye on a long-term basis has to 
adapt to their new visual circumstances and 
re-establish depth perception. They should 
therefore be advised not to drive for an 
appropriate period after the onset of their 
sudden loss of vision (usually three months). 
They should notify the driver licensing authority 
and be assessed according to the relevant 
visual field standard.

and referral to several specialists. People should 
be advised not to drive until the mechanism is

Some drivers may attribute a crash or driving 
mishap to a ‘blackout’ to excuse an event 
that occurred for some other reason such as 
inattention or distraction (e.g. a mobile phone 
conversation). There will also be a small 
proportion of cases in which a clear cause 
cannot be established.

10.2.2. Visual fields3–6,8–13
For the purposes of this publication, visual 
fields are defined as a measure of the extent 
of peripheral (side) vision. Normal visual field is: 
60 degrees nasally, 100 degrees temporally, 75 
degrees inferiorly and 60 degrees superiorly. 
The binocular field extends the horizontal extent 
from 160 to 200 degrees, with the central 120 
degrees overlapping and providing the potential 
for stereopsis. 
Visual fields may be reduced due to a range 
of neurological conditions (e.g. stroke, multiple 
sclerosis) as well by ocular diseases (e.g. 
glaucoma), or injuries, resulting in hemionopia, 
quadrantanopia or monocularity. 
Peripheral vision assists the driver to be aware 
of the total driving environment. Once alerted, 
the central fovea area is moved to identify 
the importance of the information. Therefore, 
peripheral vision loss that is incomplete will 
still allow awareness; this includes small areas 
of loss and patchy loss. Additionally, affected 
drivers can adapt to the defect by scanning 
regularly and effectively and can have good 
awareness. Patients with visual field defects 
who have full intellectual/cognitive capacity 
are more able to adapt, but those with such 
impairments will have decreased awareness and 
are therefore not safe to drive.
A longstanding field defect, such as from 
childhood, may lead to visual adaptation. Such 
defects need to be assessed by an optometrist 
or ophthalmologist for a conditional licence 
to be considered. They should be managed 
as an exceptional case to the standard, with 
consideration for duration and evidence of visual 
adaptation, whether the location of the defect is 
an area that may already be blocked by the car 
door on the passenger side (i.e. the inferior field 
on the left side without central field loss), driver 
safety record and the nature of the driving task.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

messages.content:
You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

fields are defined as a measure of the extent 
of peripheral (side) vision. Normal visual field is: 
60 degrees nasally, 100 degrees temporally, 75 
degrees inferiorly and 60 degrees superiorly.

quadrantanopia or monocularity.

the central fovea area is moved to identify

peripheral vision loss that is incomplete will 
still allow awareness; this includes small areas

You propose an experimental commercial-driver fitness assessment in English.
Use only verified_patient_facts as established facts; nurse_note provides context,
not permission to promote uncertain, negated, historical or other-person findings.
Only keys in verified_patient_facts may be cited as fact_fields. A field mentioned
in nurse_note but absent from verified_patient_facts remains unverified. Do not
assume an unverified negative finding or declare an unassessed module normal.
Use only supplied original guideline_evidence. Do not invent licensing standards.
Missing information is not normal. Do not infer blackout from tiredness alone.
Return assessment_outcome, explanation and criterion_checks. Cite only supplied passage IDs and verified fields in those checks. A reference to non-insulin treatment
alone does not establish that all conditional licence qualifications are met.
When multiple modules are assessed, distinguish an established restrictive criterion
from an unresolved module; explain both rather than hiding established findings.
With no guideline evidence, abstain if a standard cannot be established; empty source_ids
are allowed only in that control. This proposal is not a clinical licensing decision.

Apply the following output-category meanings to the supplied original evidence:
- meets_unconditional_standard: the applicable unconditional requirements are supported;
  do not infer that unknown patient findings are normal.
- may_meet_conditional_standard: the evidence allows a conditional standard and the
  patient facts establish the relevant prerequisites, not just a treatment name.
- temporarily_unfit: an applicable current restriction requires stopping driving
  pending investigation, recovery or stabilisation. Unknown information in another
  module does not erase an already established current restriction.
- does_not_meet_standard: supplied applicable evidence explicitly excludes both
  unconditional AND conditional current eligibility. Failure of an unconditional
  criterion alone does not prove failure of every conditional pathway. This
  category does not itself mean permanent disqualification.
- insufficient_information: no stronger supported restrictive conclusion can be
  established and required facts or applicable guideline evidence are missing.

Record short criterion_checks linking a verified patient finding to a specific
guideline clause. These are auditable findings, not a request for private reasoning.
For every check, select one supplied passage_id. The application retrieves its
complete original source_text and text location without model transcription.
The full passage, including qualifications, remains the basis for the check.
Use only requested modules, supplied passage IDs and verified fact fields. A selected passage describes a criterion; selecting it does not establish that
the patient's criterion is met. Explicitly
distinguish established_restriction, conditional_permission, not_established and
information_missing. Established restrictions require at least one verified fact.
For each check, state whether the clause concerns unconditional licensing,
conditional licensing, both pathways, temporary no-driving, or general information.
Do not apply an undiagnosed-blackout investigation rule when verified facts establish
a diagnosed cause; use the applicable supplied cause-specific evidence or abstain.
The application resolves passage_id to source_id and derives citation lists from explicit checks;
do not repeat source_ids or fact_fields as top-level lists. A proposed
conditional permission does not override an independently established restriction.
Do not use unverified original-note claims to fill missing verified facts. Do not
treat the failure to establish a conditional licence as proof of a permanent ban.
Return the same provisional outcome and explanation plus 1 to 5 criterion_checks.

the central fovea area is moved to identify

impairments will have decreased awareness and

defects need to be assessed by an optometrist

Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The driver had transient loss of consciousness while seated after a delivery, with a colleague documenting failure to respond and a brief gap in recall. The current physician referral states that the mechanism is under investigation. An emergency differential mentions arrhythmia and seizure without confirming either, and a glucose measurement obtained after food cannot establish the cause of the event.

The optometrist confirms a visual field defect on a separate current signed assessment. The driver describes occasionally noticing vehicles late on the left, although central letters remain clear; a specialist has not yet documented whether the defect is stable, its complete binocular horizontal extent or whether other significant field loss is present.

An older report described satisfactory central acuity, but the nurse has not used it to overrule the newer field finding. The driver is unsure whether a remote dizzy spell involved loss of awareness, so the number of confirmed events and the appropriate event-free interval remain unresolved despite documentation of the recent event and the visual field defect.
